title: Systematic graceful-degradation guard for Source implementations
description: Discovered via a real bug: LectioSource's construction path (tick-entry.ts calling lectioEnv(), which throws on missing env vars) violated the informal convention every other Source follows (construct with an empty-string env fallback, only ever throw inside fetch(), which runTick's per-source try/catch safely converts into a degradation entry). The convention is currently enforced by nothing but each Source author remembering it -- exactly the kind of thing a structural guard should catch instead. User specifically floated TS decorators as a possible mechanism (untested idea, not yet evaluated against simpler alternatives like a factory function wrapper or a lint rule). Needs real design thought before building: what's the actual guarantee to enforce (never throw synchronously in a constructor; or more specifically, never throw before fetch() is first called), what's the lightest-weight TS-native mechanism that enforces it (decorator vs factory vs lint rule vs a runtime wrapper class), and whether it's worth the complexity given there are currently only 4 Source implementations. Backlogged per user's explicit 'hold till linear, do the whole thing' instruction -- pick up alongside the other held items (pr-review-kit bundling, bot-detection-as-reusable-primitive, CI-rerun tool, fork-sync tool, worktree isolation/jj) once the linear-source build ships.
acceptance_criteria: a documented decision (not necessarily implemented) on whether/how to structurally enforce the never-throw-before-fetch convention across Source implementations

title: Adopt a shared type-driven-correctness review lens, generalized
description:
Adopts a review lens shared privately, built around the invariant-strength ranking — unrepresentable type > transaction boundary > machine-checked property > example test > prose — with three defect classes: parse-don't-validate demotions, examples where a universally-quantified property belongs, and hidden partial functions. The original author suggested generalizing it before wider use.

Generalized on three axes for this repo's agents/ registry:
1. Persona dropped. The original framed the discipline through a named practitioner while also instructing "you do not roleplay a persona; you apply a discipline" — the adoption completes that move and makes the discipline the whole identity.
2. De-repo-ified. Origin-codebase specifics became the generic patterns they instantiated — validate-then-forget, decorative wrappers, guarded-⊥ — plus a standing rule to read the target repo's own stated constraints and let them bound remedies.
3. De-language-ified where cheap. The ladder and defect classes are language-agnostic; the ⊥ hunting list is per-language (Rust, Go, TypeScript/Python) matching this ecosystem's split.

Kept in spirit: argued-vs-silent demotion as the load-bearing distinction, generator-theatre calibration, the invariant ledger output, and "no demotions worth acting on is a respectable verdict."

Frontmatter converted to this repo's Claude Code agent format, read-only tools per house convention for reviewers.

NOTE: an earlier version of this bead and its commit quoted the source material and named its origin; both were scrubbed and the commit was removed from the remote before re-landing, since this repo is public and the source was shared privately.
acceptance_criteria: agents/type-driven-correctness.md exists with house frontmatter (name/description-with-examples/model/color/tools), contains no references to the origin repo's private specifics or a named person, and is committed and pushed.

title: read_file returned empty for a missing fragment, silently blanking every consumer while the gate stayed green
description:
Found by an independent review of the include mechanism, and demonstrated against the migration landed in agents-6877ad rather than a hypothetical.

Deleting a _shared/ fragment and running `scripts/build.sh expand` removed the fragment's prose from all six consuming agents and `scripts/build.sh check` returned 0. In the reviewer's reproduction, "No findings worth acting on is a valid and respectable verdict" — the calibration guardrail — vanished from all six agents with a green gate.

Cause: read_file() in expand_file() looped `while ((getline line < p) > 0)` and returned "" for both EOF and the -1 error case, so a missing or unreadable path produced an empty replacement. check-includes could not catch it because `expand` had already written the empty version, leaving each file matching its own expansion — nothing to diff against.

The earlier mutation testing on agents-6877ad covered EDITS to a fragment and edits inside a block, both caught. It never covered DELETION of a fragment. A gate tested in one direction only.

Fixes:
1. read_file distinguishes getline's -1 from 0 and aborts with the file and fragment path named. An empty fragment also aborts, since a fragment that contributes nothing is a mistake rather than a valid state.
2. awk's exit status is captured in expand_file, so a failed read reports "include expansion aborted" rather than being misread as drift — the drift message sends the reader to `expand`, which is the command that caused the blanking.
3. read_file no longer swallows a leading blank line. The old accumulator treated out == "" as "nothing consumed yet", dropping a fragment's first line if it was empty — silent, permanent, and with no drift loop to reveal it.

Also lands the one trait extraction the review endorsed: the `**MCP dependency:** requires the rsry MCP server` line, byte-identical 6/6, into _shared/mcp-dependency-rsry.md. Verified that build.sh's body-level MCP rule survives the include (it greps the expanded file on disk, so the string is still present), and that deleting this particular fragment now fails via two independent paths.

Deliberately NOT extracted, per the review: the read-only sentence. Six phrasings, and an include would replace 1 line with 3 across 6 sites — +12 net lines to deduplicate a sentence whose payload is already carried by `disallowedTools: Write, Edit` in frontmatter and by each agent's `## Bead creation` section. Machinery exceeding payload. Unifying the wording in place remains an open editorial option, separate from extraction.</description>
<parameter name="issue_type">bug
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a _shared/ fragment makes `scripts/build.sh check-includes` exit non-zero, names the missing fragment, and leaves consuming agents unmodified; an empty fragment also fails; a fragment with a leading blank line round-trips stably; and `scripts/build.sh check` passes on the committed tree.

title: Getting-started skill: onboard a session/human to the agents repo + rosary workflow (rsry init, bead conventions, dispatch, known footguns)
description:
User request 2026-07-16: "we should also have a skill to get started for agents". Motivated by a real failure: a session hit the rsry_repo_register identity error, misdiagnosed it as an account-linking requirement, and fell back to `bd init` (banned, ADR-0014) — leaving a bd-shaped store that needed adoption/cleanup. A skill would have prevented all of it.

Ship a `getting-started` skill in this repo (skills live alongside agent definitions) covering:
1. **Onboarding a repo to rosary**: `rsry init <path>` is THE primitive (store + metadata + managed AGENTS.md + hooks + config registration, idempotent). NEVER `bd init`.
2. **The repo-tools footgun**: rsry_repo_register/rsry_repo_list are the hosted multi-tenant tier — they ALWAYS fail on local stdio ("requires user identity"); local registration is rsry init/enable/config.toml. MCP RepoPool snapshots config at boot: freshly registered repos need `repo_path` until the server restarts.
3. **Bead workflow**: search-before-create, close conditions (acceptance_criteria/test command), comment progress, `[bead-id] type(scope): description` commits (Golden Rule 11).
4. **Dispatch basics**: rsry_dispatch / rsry run --once --dry-run first; file scopes set from code reading, not title guessing.
5. **Cross-org caveat**: this repo is user-profile-owned (jamestexas) — org-installed GitHub App webhooks don't fire here; bead-close-on-merge relies on the post-merge hook (`rsry close-merged --local`).
6. **CLI cwd caveat** (until rosary-560953 lands): bead CLI ops are cwd-scoped; run them from inside the target repo or pass --repo, or results are silently empty.

Format: SKILL.md with frontmatter (name, description with trigger phrases like "onboard repo", "set up beads", "getting started with rosary"), following the conventions in this repo's existing skills.
acceptance_criteria: skills/getting-started/SKILL.md exists, covers the 6 areas above, and a fresh session following only the skill can onboard a scratch repo end-to-end (rsry init → bead create → search) without touching bd or the multi-tenant repo tools

title: Doc rot: a pointer with no target, a false tools claim, and AGENTS.md's find/replace damage
description:
Three findings from the independent review of the include mechanism, all pre-existing and unrelated to that change.

1. build.sh:148 cites CLAUDE.md "Creating new agents" as the documented home of the `**MCP dependency:**` convention it enforces. The section exists but never mentioned MCP, so the lint's only rationale pointed at nothing. Rather than weaken the pointer, the convention is now written where it claimed to be — plus a companion item on restricting tools, since prose is documentation and `disallowedTools` is enforcement.

2. CLAUDE.md said "agents inherit all tools and capabilities from the parent session, so focus on domain expertise rather than tool usage." That is false for eight agents in this repo: the six adversarial reviewers carry `disallowedTools: Write, Edit` and type-driven-correctness uses a `tools:` allowlist. It was contradicted by the same commit that wrote four of the read-only sentences. Now states the default and its exceptions.

3. AGENTS.md was produced by find/replace over CLAUDE.md, and the replacement rewrote filesystem paths and a URL as if they were product names: "Codex (Codex.ai/code)", `~/.Codex/agents/`, `.Codex/`. The real install target is `~/.claude/` for both consumers, per scripts/install.sh. Paths corrected, and the file now says it is the Codex-facing counterpart to CLAUDE.md so a convention change is known to belong in both.

NOT fixed, deliberately: CLAUDE.md:111-156 instructs `bd` usage, which this ecosystem forbids in favour of rsry. That region is a generated block (`<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION v:1 profile:minimal hash:ca08a54f -->`) carrying a content hash, so hand-editing would either be overwritten or invalidate the hash. It needs regenerating by whatever owns the block, or the block replaced with the rsry guidance AGENTS.md already carries. Left for a decision rather than patched under the marker.</description>
<parameter name="issue_type">chore
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md documents the MCP dependency convention that build.sh cites; the inherit-all-tools claim names disallowedTools/tools as exceptions; AGENTS.md contains no .Codex/ paths or Codex.ai URLs; scripts/build.sh check passes.

title: Unify the six read-only declarations, and delete the orphaned bd integration block
description:
Two editorial cleanups, kept separate from any mechanical extraction.

1. The read-only sentence varied across all six adversarial reviewers on four axes at once: bolding, opener ("You are" vs bare), joint (period vs semicolon), and a domain noun (escapes / issues / oracles / gaps / protocol bugs / compromise paths). Provenance shows this was not accreted intent — one author retyping the same sentence in a single commit, plus two older sentences left unreconciled.

The noun is redundant several times over in its own file: each agent names its domain in frontmatter description, its opening paragraph, its severity header and its bead-title template, and the noun recurs 7-27 times per file. Two of the six were already generic ("issues", "protocol bugs"), so the unified form was effectively in production in 1/6 with nobody noticing a degradation. Unified to "You are read-only. You file beads and never patch." — dropping only the redundant noun, keeping "beads" because these agents genuinely file beads and each has a ## Bead creation section.

Now byte-identical 6/6, so it would qualify for extraction under the TODO.md criteria. Deliberately NOT extracted: an include trades 1 line for 3 across 6 sites, twelve net lines to deduplicate a sentence whose payload is already carried by `disallowedTools: Write, Edit` in frontmatter and restated in each ## Bead creation section. Machinery exceeding payload. Unification alone gets the consistency; the include would only add indirection.

Excluded, per role: adversarial-synthesis-lead is the write-access integrator and has no read-only statement to unify; type-driven-correctness files findings rather than beads, uses a tools: allowlist rather than disallowedTools, and states its posture as a bullet under ## Rules.

2. Removed CLAUDE.md's `<!-- BEGIN BEADS INTEGRATION -->` block. Installed by the `bd` CLI, it instructed `bd ready` / `bd show` / `bd close` and a `bd dolt push` step — all replaced by rsry, which never invokes bd (ADR-0014). Nothing in this repository read or regenerated the block, so it was an orphan with a stale content hash contradicting AGENTS.md. Replaced with a pointer to AGENTS.md's "Issue tracking with beads" and "Landing the Plane" rather than a corrected copy: a third copy of the push discipline is how the second one came to be wrong.</description>
<parameter name="issue_type">chore
acceptance_criteria: The read-only sentence is byte-identical across the six adversarial reviewers; adversarial-synthesis-lead and type-driven-correctness are unchanged; CLAUDE.md contains no bd command instructions and no BEADS INTEGRATION markers; scripts/build.sh check passes.

title: Retrofit severity rubric, inventory step and two-sided calibration into the six adversarial agents
description:
An anatomy scan across all agents found the set strong on domain and weak on mechanism: nearly every agent has an output format, almost none has a stated procedure, a severity rubric, or a calibration warning. The six adversarial reviewers had no severity axis at all — every finding was equally weighted, which makes a report nobody can triage.

Added three parts to each, structure identical and content domain-specific:

1. A severity rubric whose assignment is a TEST, not a feeling. Each agent gets BLOCKER/COMMENT/NOTE definitions in its own domain plus a one-line rule (e.g. enumeration: "a distinction an unauthorized caller can measure is a defect; one that exists in code but yields no attacker-usable bit is a comment; an argued, disclosed leak is a note").
2. An inventory-before-reporting step: name what was examined and cleared, not only what yielded findings, so coverage is checkable and a thorough pass is distinguishable from a lucky one.
3. A two-sided calibration warning naming both failure modes — the agent's specific zealotry mode and its specific credulity mode — closing with explicit permission that "no findings worth acting on" is a valid and respectable verdict.

Also replaces "lens" with house terminology throughout. agents/ never used the word; the six say "adversarial reviewer specializing in X" and skills/survey establishes "perspective" as the structural term (--perspectives, perspective:prod bead labels). "Lens" arrived with an externally-sourced agent and is now gone from agents/ entirely.</description>
<parameter name="issue_type">chore
acceptance_criteria: All six adversarial agents contain a `## Severity` section with a stated assignment rule, an inventory-before-reporting instruction, and a `## Calibration` section naming both failure modes; `grep -ri lens agents/` returns nothing.

title: work-board drops recurring same-titled events from the render — synthesized identity is not unique
description:
normalizeBoard synthesized artifactUri as kind:repo#number-or-title, falling back to the TITLE when no number exists. Calendar events carry neither repo nor number, so every occurrence of a recurring meeting got the identical key 'event:local#standup'.

render.ts joins on artifactUri as D3's key (lines 192 and 241). Duplicate keys are dropped from a D3 join rather than drawn over each other, so the second and later occurrences were never rendered. The board looked right — that is what made it hard to see.

dialLayout compounded it: it recovered an item's position with group.findIndex(e => e.artifactUri === item.artifactUri), which returns the FIRST match, so duplicates were also assigned one angle.

Proved before fixing: two same-titled standups both produced 'event:local#standup' and both landed at angle 81.

Fixed at the source — a number is left as the discriminator (appending activity there would break D3 object constancy and re-enter a PR on every update), and the occurrence time is added only where the title was all there was. dialLayout now records position during grouping, keyed by object identity, so it no longer depends on identities being unique.

Found while reading work-board as the reference pattern for hosting 0day's MCP server as a cloister bundle (0day-bd65c6).
acceptance_criteria: Two same-titled events with no repo/number get distinct artifactUris and distinct dial angles; a numbered artifact's identity does not change when its activity does. Verified by mutation.

title: wait-for-ci-rerun: mechanical CI re-trigger tool, for after a human/agent judges a failure flaky
description: User pattern: 'retriggering flaky CI (if we determine it's flaky, this is subjective and the operation is a tool)' -- same mechanistic-gather/probabilistic-discuss/mechanistic-submit shape as wait-for-pr (already shipped this session at ~/.local/bin/wait-for-pr). Determining flakiness is a judgment call (read the failure, decide if it's a real bug or infra flake) -- but the ACTION of re-running CI once decided is pure mechanism: gh run rerun / gh run rerun --failed for GitHub Actions (or equivalent for whatever CI system is in play per-repo). Design like wait-for-pr: single command, no output until done, safe to background. Should probably compose with wait-for-pr -- e.g. wait-for-pr --rerun-if-flaky, or a separate rerun-ci command that wait-for-pr can chain into.
acceptance_criteria: a new ~/.local/bin script (or wait-for-pr extension) that mechanically re-runs failed CI checks on a PR given an explicit go-ahead, matching wait-for-pr's silent-until-done convention

title: sync-branch: mechanize the fetch/stash/checkout-main/pull/checkout-back/rebase git recipe, pause only at conflicts
description: User's exact described workflow, currently fully manual: 'Sync fork (don't lose current branch state) -> git fetch -> stash -> checkout main -> pull -> checkout branch -> rebase -> resolve conflicts -> push -> tell Claude it's ok I did it'. Every step except 'resolve conflicts' is pure mechanism -- the user currently does the WHOLE thing by hand and only tells Claude once it's done, rather than delegating the mechanical bookend steps and only handling (or being handed) the judgment part. Design: a script that runs fetch/stash/checkout-main/pull/checkout-branch/rebase automatically, and EITHER pauses cleanly with clear state if rebase hits a conflict (leaving the repo in a normal mid-rebase state the user or Claude can resolve), or completes straight through (stash-pop, done) if no conflicts. Should NOT auto-push -- that's likely still a separate, explicit step given push is broadly considered higher-stakes than a local rebase.
acceptance_criteria: a new ~/.local/bin script that mechanizes fetch->stash->checkout main->pull->checkout branch->rebase, stopping cleanly at a real conflict rather than needing the whole recipe done by hand

Do not execute gh from the UI Worker or duplicate subprocess behavior inside workerd.
